stock: 205/75R15 (≈ 27.1 in tall), the factory size per The Ranger Station

max_tire.note: Shown on The Ranger Station with no lift and trimmed fenders. Its rule of thumb pairs 31s with about 1.5 in of lift plus trimming. The Dana 28 front axle is rated for about 31 in tires.
Fits with the bottom rear corner of the front fender trimmed.

max_tire.size: 31–32 in (33 in with cut-out flares or a 3 in body lift)
max_tire.note: The Ranger Station's chart: 31s fit, 32s need trimming, and 33s need cut-out flares or a 3 in body lift.

max_tire.size: 33 in (35 in with a 2–3 in body lift and cut-out flares)
max_tire.note: 35s also show up on 3–5.5 in lifts with body lifts and cut-out flares, and on solid-axle swaps. At this size, plan for a Dana 35 or a solid axle, an 8.8 rear and regearing.

items.title: Shoulder-belt D-ring anchorage too weak
items.summary: The D-ring mounting didn't meet FMVSS 210; dealers installed stronger attaching hardware.

items.title: Automatic locking-hub cams may crack
items.summary: Improperly heat-treated hub components could fracture when the front axle engaged; cam assemblies were replaced.

items.title: EEC wiring harness short can open fuel injectors
items.summary: Welding spikes could damage harness insulation and short the fuel-pump circuit, discharging fuel into the engine; the harness was repaired and the engine and catalyst checked.

items.title: Nylon fuel-return lines may crack
items.summary: Lines on the return side of the pressure regulator could crack and leak; they were replaced with rubber hoses.

items.title: Spring-lock fuel couplings may not be engaged
items.summary: Dealers installed retainer clips over the couplings to prevent separation and fuel leaks.

items.title: Wrong lug nuts on aluminum wheels
items.summary: Tapered lug nuts were replaced with the correct short-shank type.

items.title: Handling-warning sticker on the sun visor won't stay on
items.summary: The handling and maneuverability decal didn't meet the permanent-adhesion requirement; owners were mailed new visor sleeves with the warning printed on.

items.title: Power lumbar seat wiring can chafe
items.summary: Wiring routed under the seat springs could be abraded; a fuse was added to the circuit.

items.title: Front wheel-bearing nut retaining keys missing
items.summary: Without the keys the adjusting nut could loosen; dealers installed them where missing.

items.title: Automatic transmission park pawl may not engage
items.summary: The park pawl didn't always engage the park gear; transmissions were repaired with a new pawl.

timeline.change: Production begins at Louisville in January and the Bronco II is introduced in March as a 1984 model. Four-wheel drive only, carbureted 2.8 Cologne V6 (115 hp), TK4 four-speed or C5 automatic, Dana 28 TTB, 7.5 rear.

Five-speed manuals (TK5, FM145); the A4LD four-speed automatic replaces the C5 from November 1984 builds; power window and lock group; side glass changes from glued to bolted-in late in the year. Last year of the XLS.

Fuel-injected 2.9 Cologne V6 (140 hp); Mitsubishi 2.3 turbodiesel offered; Touch-Drive electric-shift transfer case late in the year. The Ranger Station says 1986–88 2.9 heads are known to crack, and rates 1985–87 A4LD automatics the least reliable.
Rear-wheel ABS standard; 2WD sales begin in earnest (22,286 sold per NHTSA). Still crack-prone 2.9 heads and the early A4LD, which The Ranger Station's builder's guide says to stay away from.
Sequential fuel injection; FM146 and Mazda M5OD five-speeds; dual-solenoid A4LD from mid-year; XL Sport arrives. Last year of the front-door vent windows and the early body.

Facelift to match the Ranger: new hood, fenders, bumper and dashboard, 161.9 in long. Redesigned 89TM 2.9 heads largely eliminate the cracking, and The Ranger Station rates 1989-on A4LDs noticeably better than 1985–87. Ball joints move from the TTB beam to the knuckle. XLT Plus package.

Final year, with the 89TM heads. BW1354 on electric-shift trucks; Dana 35 TTB on 4x4s built from November 1989; some 2WD trucks get a true 2WD transmission. Production ends in early 1990 and the Explorer replaces it for 1991.

identify.intro: Nearly every Bronco II has been modified or had parts swapped from Rangers and Explorers, so identification is mostly about which drivetrain is fitted now and which it left the factory with.

items.head: Door-post label codes
items.body: The Federal Safety Compliance Certification label on the driver's door post lists the axle code (ratio and limited slip) and the TRANS code. Ranger Station manual-transmission codes include X (TK4), 5 (TK5), D (FM145/FM146) and M (M5OD); automatics are W (C5) and T (A4LD).

items.head: Front axle
items.body: A Dana 28 TTB has a 12-bolt cover, 23-spline shafts and a date code beginning with E. A Dana 35 has a 10-bolt cover, 27-spline shafts and an F code. Only 1990 trucks built from November 1989 came with a Dana 35, so on anything earlier it's a swap.

items.head: 2WD or 4WD
items.body: A 2WD truck usually still has a transfer-case-shaped BW1359 behind a 4WD-style transmission, but no front driveshaft or front differential. Late 1990 2WD trucks may have a true 2WD transmission with a bolt-on flange adapter instead.

items.head: Engine and heads
items.body: The 2.8 (1984–85) is carbureted with a gear-driven cam. The 2.9 (1986–90) has an upper intake reading "2.9L Electronic Fuel Injection". Improved heads have rectangular rocker pedestals and 89TM castings; early heads have oval pedestals.

items.head: Eddie Bauer
items.body: 1984–88 trucks are two-tone over Light Desert Tan with Eddie Bauer fender badges, a logo on the passenger side of the dash and a tan interior with pine-tree stitching. 1989–90 trucks are two-tone over Light Sandalwood and have a signature decal instead of a badge, plus striped seats with Eddie Bauer and duck headrest graphics.

items.head: Early-build clues
items.body: Removable flip-out quarter windows appeared only on early 1983.5 production. Glued-in side glass with metal trim means a 1984 to early-1985 build. Front-door vent windows ended in 1988. A 1984 fuel tank has a smaller sending-unit opening than 1985–90 tanks.

capability.v: 23.8 cu ft behind the rear seat · 57 cu ft maximum

capability.note: Factory-era ratings: a 1984 4x4 with the 2.8 and C5 automatic was 15/17; the best was a 1986–88 2WD five-speed 2.9 at 17/22

values.intro: Bronco IIs are still cheap. Clean, original Eddie Bauers and XLT 4x4 five-speeds bring the most, and very-low-mileage survivors bring far more.

ranges.cond: Good original XLT or Eddie Bauer 4x4

values.note: Based on 24 recent Bring a Trailer results (August 2024 to October 2026): sold prices ran from $5,000 (a 302-swapped 1989 XLT) to $15,750 for most trucks, with a 9,000-mile 1989 Eddie Bauer at $28,550. BaT lists 69 Bronco II auctions in all.
